html-in-canvas

Web·by @rpavlini·2026-08-19·inspora page·original post

What it is

html-in-canvas: a 'Coming soon' shop teaser rendered in canvas - a pile of hand-drawn sticker/stamp artwork ('1779 CASEMATES SQUARE', 'LY BATTERY SURVIVORS CLUB', 'Lo-Fi', 'GIBRALTAR') sits center page and a large glass sphere acts as a draggable magnifying lens: it refracts and enlarges whatever artwork passes beneath it with chromatic rim fringes; copy: 'Meanwhile, click, drag and explore'; light and dark page variants.

## Integration
Integration: stack-agnostic spec - springs given as stiffness/damping, timed motions as duration + curve, canvas/shader notes are perf guidance only; map every value to your framework and animation library of choice.

## Scene
Center: a pile of overlapping hand-drawn stickers/stamps. A large glass sphere parked over the pile; whatever is beneath bulges enlarged inside it, rainbow dispersion at the glass rim. Page copy invites dragging. Dark-mode variant: sphere picks up the environment tint; a settings panel at the right in dark frames.

## Motion spec
Pattern: draggable lens.
- Drag: sphere follows the pointer 1:1 across the pile; artwork warps and swells through the lens with barrel refraction; rim fringe (chromatic dispersion) constant.
- Release: sphere glides with slight inertia and settles (300ms).
- Parked on artwork (e.g. the "Lo-Fi" script sticker): that art renders hugely magnified inside the sphere; the surrounding pile stays static.

## Calibration
- Magnification ~1.5-2x inside the sphere with barrel distortion toward the rim - a lens, not a zoom window.
- Refraction responds in real time; any lag in the lens content destroys the glass illusion.
- Rim fringe is thin and constant; a thick rainbow reads as a soap bubble.

## Reduced motion
Sphere moves 1:1 (positional) but shows plain magnification without distortion or fringe.

## Don't miss
- The lens samples the ACTUAL artwork beneath it in real time - pre-baked zoomed images will misalign.
- The sticker pile has casual overlap and rotation; a tidy grid kills the hand-drawn energy.
- Dark mode tints the sphere's glass; it participates in the theme.
